machine.fs_caveat: Timings were taken on a tmpfs scratch copy; the real repository lives on ext4. Filesystem-metadata costs (lock-file creation, fsync, atomic rename) are UNDERSTATED here. The dominant cost (minor page faults / memory materialization) is filesystem-independent and reproduces on any backing store.

corpus.source: scratch copy of the jit repository's own .jit/ (dogfood data), .git and .jit copied with cp -a

method.tool: python3 subprocess timing loop (hyperfine/strace/perf-trace unavailable in this environment)
method.cache_state: warm (page cache primed by warmup runs); cold-cache not measured because dropping page cache needs root
method.syscall_profile_tool: perf stat -e task-clock,context-switches,page-faults,minor-faults (perf trace / strace blocked by perf_event_paranoid=2 and no CAP_SYS_ADMIN)

commands.name: issue_show_single_read
commands.note: reads one issue via load_issue; creates the target issue's sidecar .lock (json.rs:918)

commands.name: query_available
commands.note: list_issues -> load_issue per id -> one sidecar .lock per issue

commands.name: issue_update_mutation
commands.note: two full in-memory repository captures per mutation; corroborates the audit's uncorroborated 3.747s figure

mutation_syscall_summary.interpretation: System-time and minor-page-fault dominated. 545219 minor faults * 4KiB ~= 2.1 GiB of memory touched for a single-issue mutation. context-switches=0 rules out a blocking git subprocess. A title-only mutation costs the same (~3.67s), so the cost is the base two-full-capture materialization, not the auto-transition-to-Done recursion or lock I/O (only 1 lock created).

lock_mechanism.creator: FileLocker::open_or_create (crates/jit/src/storage/lock.rs:286-294) opens O_CREAT
lock_mechanism.never_removed: LockGuard::drop (crates/jit/src/storage/lock.rs:66-75) only unlocks and removes the .lock.meta; the .lock file itself persists
lock_mechanism.cleanup_scope: cleanup_stale_locks (crates/jit/src/storage/lock_cleanup.rs:67) runs only over the claims lock dir (.git/jit/locks), never over .jit/issues/*.lock
lock_mechanism.gitignored: .jit/**/*.lock (.gitignore:5) — never tracked, but accumulates on disk unbounded
lock_mechanism.writes_are_atomic: issue JSON is published via atomic_write.rs::write_file_atomic (temp file + fs::rename, atomic_write.rs:365); writers serialize on .jit/.repo-write.lock; list_issues already holds .index.lock shared (json.rs:1029) around the whole load loop, so the per-issue sidecar read lock is redundant
